skill.name: github-release-management
skill.description: Orchestrates GitHub releases with version planning, changelog creation, CI validation, artifact publishing, rollout monitoring, and rollback guidance.
skill.summary: Guide GitHub releases from version planning through validation, publishing, announcements, and rollback.
skill.author: Claude Flow Team

security_audit.summary: Most backtick and hardcoded URL detections are Markdown documentation examples, not hidden runtime code. Confirmed risks remain in the privileged GitHub Actions examples: unpinned alpha CLI execution, broad write permissions, token handling, and predictable temporary files. No prompt injection attempt was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Unpinned alpha release tooling runs in CI.
remediation.suggestion: Pin claude-flow to a reviewed version or digest, and verify the package before use in release jobs.

remediation.issue: Release job has broad write permissions.
remediation.suggestion: Scope GitHub Actions permissions by job and step, and require protected environments for publishing.

remediation.issue: Publishing tokens are written or persisted during workflow steps.
remediation.suggestion: Use scoped tokens, avoid long-lived workspace token files, and remove .npmrc immediately after publishing.

remediation.issue: Predictable files under /tmp feed release note generation.
remediation.suggestion: Use mktemp or RUNNER_TEMP with restrictive permissions, then validate file ownership before reading.

remediation.issue: Emergency hotfix automation can start from issue label events.
remediation.suggestion: Require environment approvals or maintainer confirmation before any fast-track release or publish step.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Alpha Release Tooling in Privileged CI
semantic_findings.description: The release workflow runs npx claude-flow@alpha during privileged release steps. A changed or compromised alpha package could run with repository and package publishing access.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow explicitly uses @alpha in CI release steps that also authenticate GitHub and npm publishing. This is a direct supply-chain risk, not just a generic command example.

semantic_findings.title: Overbroad Workflow Write Permissions
semantic_findings.description: The release workflow grants contents, packages, and issues write permissions to the whole release job. Any compromised step can mutate releases, publish packages, or create issues.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The permissions block is explicit and applies to a job that runs many shell and third-party CLI steps. Least-privilege scoping is not shown.

semantic_findings.title: Issue Label Can Trigger Fast-Track Hotfix Automation
semantic_findings.description: The hotfix workflow starts from issue label events and runs emergency release automation with a fast-track flag. This can bypass normal release gates if label permissions are broad.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The trigger and fast-track command are present, but actual exploitability depends on repository label permissions and default workflow token settings.

high_findings.title: Shell command substitution
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow captures output from npx claude-flow@alpha during release generation. Running an unpinned alpha package in CI can execute changed package code with release privileges.

content.value_statement: Release work often spans versions, changelogs, validation, artifacts, and announcements. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through structured GitHub release workflows.
actual_capabilities: Provides GitHub CLI flows for draft releases, release notes, and published releases.
Shows semantic version, changelog, and migration-guide workflows.
Outlines Claude Flow swarm roles for release planning, testing, and review.
Includes GitHub Actions examples for release and emergency hotfix pipelines.
Covers validation, artifact publishing, announcements, monitoring, and rollback steps.
limitations: Requires GitHub CLI, git, Node.js, and npm or yarn in the target project.
Assumes the user has repository, package, and workflow permissions.
Uses placeholder versions, repositories, and package names that need project-specific review.
Example CI workflows require security hardening before production use.

use_cases.title: Plan a Standard Release
use_cases.description: Create a version plan, changelog outline, validation list, and release draft for a single repository.

use_cases.title: Coordinate a Monorepo Release
use_cases.description: Align package versions, run cross-package checks, and prepare a shared release pull request.

use_cases.title: Run an Emergency Hotfix
use_cases.description: Prepare a focused hotfix path with critical tests, release notes, stakeholder updates, and rollback checks.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Release Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a GitHub release for version v2.0.0. Include version rationale, changelog sections, validation steps, and approval checkpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Release Notes
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate release notes from merged pull requests and commits since the last tag. Group changes by features, fixes, breaking changes, and documentation.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Release Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this GitHub Actions release workflow. Identify missing validation, unsafe permissions, secret handling risks, and rollback gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate a Multi-Package Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a coordinated release for several packages in one repository. Include dependency ordering, compatibility checks, publishing sequence, and rollback strategy.

output_examples.input: Plan release v2.0.0 for a Node.js package with breaking changes.
output_examples.output: A release plan with version rationale, freeze dates, required tests, changelog sections, approval steps, and rollback criteria.

output_examples.input: Summarize merged work since v1.9.0 for release notes.
output_examples.output: A categorized release note draft covering features, fixes, breaking changes, migration guidance, contributors, and known issues.

output_examples.input: Check whether a hotfix release process is ready.
output_examples.output: A readiness review covering branch source, targeted tests, artifact validation, publishing permissions, communication steps, and rollback readiness.

best_practices: Review every generated command before execution in a real repository.
Use least-privilege tokens and require protected environments for publishing.
Pin release tooling versions and verify artifacts before publication.
anti_patterns: Running unpinned release tooling in CI with repository write permissions.
Publishing packages before tests, changelog review, and release approval finish.
Leaving package registry tokens in workspace files after publishing.

faq.question: Does this skill create releases automatically?
faq.answer: It provides structured guidance and command examples. Users should review and approve commands before execution.

faq.question: Which repositories does it support?
faq.answer: It is designed for GitHub repositories that use GitHub CLI, GitHub Actions, and common Node.js release tooling.

faq.question: Can it manage monorepos?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes examples for coordinating versions, dependencies, tests, and release pull requests across packages.

faq.question: Does it replace CI testing?
faq.answer: No. It helps plan and invoke validation, but the project must provide reliable test and build commands.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Use scoped secrets, protected environments, and cleanup steps. Avoid storing tokens in workspace files longer than needed.

faq.question: Is it safe for production workflows?
faq.answer: The guidance is useful, but example workflows need pinning, permission review, and secret-handling hardening before production use.
